note: Replace each `url` below with a Stripe Payment Link from the parish Stripe dashboard, then set `configured` to true. Payment Links are public URLs — never place a Stripe secret key (sk_live_… / sk_test_…) in this repository.

demo.note: Renders an interactive mock of the checkout so the parish can review the donor experience and compare providers before committing. No card is ever charged and no payment API is called. `publishableKey` is Stripe's own sample TEST key from their public documentation; publishable keys are designed to be readable by anyone and cannot move money. Set `enabled` to false to hide the mock.

zelle.note: Set this to the email address or phone number enrolled with the parish bank account once Zelle is set up. Until it is filled in, the Zelle panel says so rather than inventing an address.

providersNote: Comparison data for the provider selector on the Giving page. Cursory analysis, September 2026, verified against vendor documentation rather than live accounts — see docs/giving-setup.md. `status` drives the colour: yes / no / partial / info.

providers.name: Stripe
providers.tagline: Best engineering platform and by far the cheapest bank transfers, but it cannot do a donor-chosen monthly amount without a workaround.

specs.label: API layer required
specs.value: No for Payment Links; yes to embed checkout on our own page

specs.label: Donor-chosen recurring amount
specs.value: No — needs fixed tiers or a quantity workaround

specs.label: Works on a static site
specs.value: Yes — redirect to a hosted page

caveats: Non-profit processing rates are lower than the list price above, but must be requested once the account is verified.

providers.name: Square
providers.tagline: The only one of the three that lets a donor name their own amount and repeat it monthly with no code — the exact gap Stripe has.

specs.label: Recurring donations
specs.value: Yes — donation links take a one-time or recurring frequency

specs.label: Works on a static site
specs.value: Yes — redirect to a hosted page

caveats: The $5,000 cap could block a large building gift. Those would need an invoice instead.
Square's non-profit rate appears to apply to Invoices rather than to all online donations. Confirm before switching.
Best fit if the parish ever wants one system covering the bookstore, candle desk, and online giving.

providers.name: Donorbox
providers.tagline: Rents someone else's backend. Everything works out of the box, including donor-chosen recurring, at the highest price of the four.

specs.label: API layer required
specs.value: No — Donorbox is the API layer

specs.label: Works on a static site
specs.value: Yes — an iframe that stays on our page

caveats: The 2.95% platform fee sits on top of Stripe's processing, so a $100 monthly tithe nets about $94.55 against roughly $97.50 on Stripe alone.
The Pro plan cuts the platform fee to 1.75% for $150 a month, which only breaks even above roughly $12,500 of donations a month — far beyond this parish.
This is how github.com/jeffch19/paal-nonprofit-website does recurring giving on GitHub Pages: it embeds a Donorbox iframe rather than integrating Stripe itself.

providers.name: Zelle
providers.tagline: Genuinely free, which is real money on large gifts — but it cannot be integrated into a website at all.

specs.label: API layer required
specs.value: No integration is possible at all

specs.label: Recurring donations
specs.value: Only if the donor schedules it in their own bank app

specs.label: Donor-chosen recurring amount
specs.value: Yes, but the parish cannot set it up or change it

specs.label: Automatic receipts
specs.value: None — the treasurer issues them manually

specs.label: Per-transaction cap
specs.value: Set by the donor's bank, often $1,000–$3,500 a day

specs.label: Works on a static site
specs.value: No form to embed; we publish an address

caveats: A $5,000 building donation costs about $145 in card fees and nothing by Zelle, so it is worth publishing alongside a card option rather than instead of one.
Not all banks offer Zelle on business or non-profit accounts. Confirm with the parish bank first.
No donor data comes through, so gift-aid style records and year-end statements are entirely manual.
